findings.title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never consumed and can be replayed
findings.body: For locally stored recovery-code credentials, the credential provider's isValid() consumes the used code (removes it from the credential data), making each code one-time-use. With this PR, when the credential lives in user storage, validation via user.credentialManager().isValid() delegates to the storage provider's isValid(realm, user, input), which can only check membership and has no way to remove the used code (see the new BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid, which just does generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...) without updating anything). As a result, a recovery code stored in federated user storage remains valid forever and can be replayed by anyone who captured it, defeating the one-time-use semantics that are the entire point of recovery codes. Additionally, the cleanup logic here never helps: allCodesUsed() will never become true because the credential data is never updated, and even if it were, removeStoredCredentialById() only removes locally stored credentials and silently does nothing for a federated credential.

findings.title: Optional.get() crashes when user storage supports recovery codes but does not expose them via getCredentials
findings.body: The bean now calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user), which looks at getFederatedCredentialsStream() and then local storage, and immediately calls .get() on the Optional. However, the authenticator's configuredFor() uses credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(TYPE), which for user storage delegates to the provider's isConfiguredFor()/supportsCredentialType(). A user storage provider can legitimately implement CredentialInputUpdater + CredentialInputValidator (so it reports the credential as configured and can validate it) without implementing the optional CredentialInputProvider interface that backs getFederatedCredentialsStream(). For such a provider, getCredential() returns Optional.empty() and credentialModelOpt.get() throws NoSuchElementException, producing a server error instead of the recovery-code login page. The same mismatch affects RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator's post-validation lookup. The code should handle the empty Optional instead of assuming presence.

findings.title: No test that a used recovery code is invalidated, and no test for the local-storage fallback
findings.body: The new testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only verifies one successful login with a recovery code. It never attempts to reuse the same code, which is exactly the scenario that is broken for user-storage-backed recovery codes (the storage's isValid cannot consume the used code, so reuse currently succeeds). A test asserting that the second login attempt with the same code fails would have caught the replay flaw. Additionally, the fallback path in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential (user storage's updateCredential returns false, credential is created in the Keycloak DB via the recovery-codes credential provider) is not exercised anywhere: the only modified test storage now always supports the recovery-codes type, so a regression in the local-storage path would go unnoticed.
